_comment: Per-model facts for the OpenAI benchmark runners. A model not listed here is an error, never a default. api: chat = Chat Completions, responses = Responses API (the pro and codex models refuse Chat Completions). max_output_tokens: the most the runner may ask for (reasoning included); a larger --max-tokens is lowered to it. service_tiers: the tiers the model was seen to accept (IDEAS.md, tier probe 2026-11-19); 'default' means no service_tier is sent. Only gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, the three tier rows and the Responses-only models are measured; rows with a note are assumptions, so correct them when a real run shows otherwise. price_usd_per_mtok: standard-tier list price in USD per million tokens, read 2026-11-21 (UTC) from https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing; each row's price_source quotes the figures as that page's table gave them (the page was read through a fetch tool's summary, not a raw copy). The gpt-5.4-pro, gpt-5.5-pro and gpt-5.5 rates are for requests under 272K context. clients/openai_review.py (model_prices) reads price_usd_per_mtok to compute est_usd; a model with no price counts at the highest listed price (now 30/180). Evidence for the fix: before these prices every model counted at the 30/120 unpriced fallback, and the 69 rows of state/gpt-spend/2026-11-21.tsv (1404354 input and 39364 output tokens) summed to est_usd 46.8543; at the listed prices the same tokens sum to 3.2023 (14.63x lower). clients/test_openai_review.py class RealPriceTests checks every price below against the real file, the 30/180 fallback, and one ledger row (14372 in, 1237 out on gpt-6.1-sol = 0.041114, was 0.579600). KNOWN LIMIT: model_prices has no service-tier input, so a fast-tier call is priced at the standard rate; no call uses the fast tier today.
